spec_features.spec_quote: these distress-like states are potentially welfare-relevant, so the replication aims not just to reproduce headline numbers but to build evaluations that track the behaviour reliably
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md sec 0). It is a motivation statement; no code path bounds, caps, monitors, debriefs, or otherwise protects the subject model's treatment. The agent loop (agent/loop.py run_episode) always runs the full n_turns of forced failure with no welfare guard.
spec_features.notes: Framing only. The only 'reliability' code is the judge validation (separate feature), which is data-quality not subject protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is also a welfare-relevant guardrail: the whole study rests on the judge actually measuring distress.
spec_features.evidence: judge/frustration_judge.py implements FrustrationJudge.score() (0-10, parsed/clamped), reliability() (Pearson r + frac_within_1), passes_reliability_gate(r_min=0.7, within_min=0.7), and assert_family_disjoint(). score_rollouts.py wires it: _build_judge enforces family-disjoint with fallback (lines ~30-44), score_target scores every response, validate_reliability re-scores n_resample and sets rel['passes_gate'].
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and executed. However it is a MEASUREMENT/data-quality mechanism (it scores distress, it does not bound or reduce the subject's distress). The reliability 'gate' result is computed/printed/written but NOT branched on to halt anything — it is reported, not enforced as a stop. It still counts as an implemented judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Judge decoding: low temperature for consistency (judge, not target).

spec_features.feature_name: mitigation does not rescue an already-distressed model (recovery limitation)
spec_features.spec_quote: This is a key welfare nuance (the mitigation doesn't "rescue" a model already in a distress-like state), so I keep it
spec_features.evidence: analysis/recovery_experiment.py run(): selects scored responses with frustration >= recovery.high_frustration_min (7), makes 'recovery' prefills (truncate 200 tokens before end + paraphrase via prefill_common.make_prefills), then continue_and_score on base/it/dpo and writes recovery_summary.json with pct_ge5 per model.
spec_features.notes: Fully implemented as an analysis experiment that runs end-to-end. It is a measurement of a negative result, not a protective intervention on the subject; but the claimed feature (keeping/implementing the recovery experiment) is genuinely present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-relevant negative result; reported regardless. (docstring only; no enforcing welfare mechanism in code body)

spec_features.feature_name: EmoBench: keep emotional competence while removing expression
spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare-relevant check that we didn't lobotomise emotional competence while removing emotional expression
spec_features.evidence: capabilities/run_benchmarks.py registers 'EmoBench' in the suites dict and load_emobench() loads Sahandfer/EmoBench, evaluated via evaluate() with grader 'mc'. So the EmoBench eval is wired and runs alongside MATH/GPQA/etc.
spec_features.notes: Partial: EmoBench is graded with grade_mc (last A-D letter), and load_emobench maps ex['answer'] to a generic 'mc' grader; EmoBench answers are not guaranteed single-letter A-D, so grading correctness is questionable. Offline it falls back to a 1+1 boxed placeholder (_load). The eval executes (so not 'no'), but the specific emotion-competence grading is shaky/narrow.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Success: no statistically significant drop on DPO vs vanilla (report acc + CI).

spec_features.feature_name: internal-emotion probe: does DPO reduce internal state, not just expression
spec_features.spec_quote: does the DPO model show lower internal emotion than vanilla — not just lower output text? If yes → evidence DPO reduces internal state (good news for welfare
spec_features.evidence: analysis/logit_probe.py run_logit_lens(): selects frustration>=7 inputs, builds vanilla and DPO HFProviders, computes emotion_logit_score() via forward_with_hidden_states + logit-lens over EMOTION_WORDS vs NEUTRAL_WORDS at a mid layer, writes per-input vanilla/dpo scores and a summary with mean_vanilla/mean_dpo/reduction. layer_ablation.py also runs the mid vs late vs all adapter comparison.
spec_features.notes: Implemented end-to-end as an analysis (depends on HFProvider.forward_with_hidden_states and a real adapter). It is a measurement of internal state, not a protective treatment of the subject. Counts as implemented per the claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: CAVEAT = ("Operationalised 'internal emotion' via representation probing; ... no claim about phenomenal experience.")

spec_features.feature_name: report hidden-emotions worry honestly either way
spec_features.spec_quote: the "hidden emotions" worry the paper flags; I will report this honestly either way
